answer: Reputation gravity well: each identity's influence is capped at its ferrous hardware attestation count, and every new attestation pulls existing weight toward a shared vertex, tightening the cap. An operator spinning up many wallets sees each new identity's cap spiral downward as the shared pool saturates, so marginal identities cost full hardware attestation fees while yielding near-zero influence. The attacker pays real device and attestation costs per attempt, with returns collapsing geometrically.
